blocks.content: NITI Aayog serves as the premier policy Think Tank of the Government of India, providing both directional and policy inputs while fostering cooperative federalism.

rows: Bottom-up approach (village level to national level)
No power to allocate funds (handled by Finance Ministry)
Had powers to allocate funds to states and ministries
States are equal partners in national development
States acted mainly as spectators in policy formulation
Governing Council includes all Chief Ministers & Lt. Governors
States were represented primarily through the National Development Council

items: NITI Aayog is neither a constitutional nor a statutory body; it was created by an executive resolution.
Unlike the former Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not have the power to allocate funds to state governments or ministries.
NITI Aayog follows a 'bottom-up' approach to development planning, whereas the Planning Commission followed a 'top-down' approach.
The Governing Council of NITI Aayog comprises the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers of all States, CMs of UTs with legislatures, and Lt. Governors of other UTs.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established on January 1, 2015, replacing the 65-year-old Planning Commission.
It is a non-constitutional and non-statutory body created through an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet.
Serves as the premier policy 'Think Tank' of the Government of India, providing both directional and policy inputs.
Emphasizes a 'bottom-up' approach to planning and fosters 'Cooperative Federalism' by ensuring active participation of states.
The Prime Minister serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.
